own_scenes.desc: Tras los disturbios de Los Ángeles, el hip hop chocó con los políticos y los intereses corporativos. Bill Clinton, con Al Gore (marido de Tipper) de compañero, condenó una frase sacada de contexto de la activista Sister Souljah, cercana a Public Enemy: el «momento Sister Souljah». La policía pidió boicotear a Time Warner por «Cop Killer» de Body Count, el grupo de heavy metal de Ice-T, aunque no era hip hop: en la junta de accionistas de julio de 1992 Charlton Heston, en nombre de la NRA, leyó en voz alta «KKK Bitch»; el consejero delegado Gerald Levin solo invocó la Primera Enmienda. Ice-T retiró la canción por las amenazas a empleados y Warner empezó a filtrar letras y portadas: no distribuyó Live and Let Die de Kool G Rap & DJ Polo y bloqueó Sleeping with the Enemy de Paris («Bush Killa»), cuya portada filtró una ayudante de Tommy Boy de familia de policías. Ice-T se marchó por la portada de Home Invasion; a Paris lo despidieron el mismo día que a Ice-T y a G Rap, cobró cien mil dólares y sus másteres y fundó Scarface Records: seis dólares y medio por disco en vez de cincuenta céntimos.

influences.name: Ice-T y el reality rap de Los Ángeles

refs.q: That whole “Cop Killer” shit was a bunch of bullshit. It was just meant to be a record.
refs.para: Ice-T (artist, Body Count): That whole “Cop Killer” shit was a bunch of bullshit. It was just meant to be a record. It wasn’t meant to be some political platform to say anything.

refs.q: There’s nothing like hearing Charlton Heston get up in the back of the Beverly Wilshire and start reciting “KKK Bitch.”
refs.para: Monica Lynch (president, Tommy Boy Records): There’s nothing like hearing Charlton Heston get up in the back of the Beverly Wilshire and start reciting “KKK Bitch.” That was one for the ages.

refs.q: That’s your pull quote. It was a fucking mess.
refs.para: When she didn’t show up for work, then I was like, I think I know what happened here. But it was a fucking mess. That’s your pull quote. It was a fucking mess.

refs.q: It forced me to realize the importance of being independent, and the importance of control.
refs.para: Paris (artist, producer, San Francisco): It was a blessing in disguise, honestly. It forced me to realize the importance of being independent, and the importance of control. It was trial by fire, basically. I delivered the project, then I delivered the artwork. There was a lot of publicity that had been put in place when the outcry from Ice-T’s “Cop Killer” boiled over and forced everybody who had anything incendiary to say to be released from their respective contracts.
